passage:
A museum exhibit showed medical tools from different periods. Some looked useful. Others looked painful or strange.
The guide explained that people in the past often worked with limited knowledge. Some treatments helped. Some harmed. Medical progress came from observation, testing, and correcting mistakes.
Students compared old tools with modern ones and felt grateful, but also thoughtful.
The guide warned them not to laugh too quickly. Future people may look back at today's medicine and see limits too.
Science improves by admitting it does not know everything yet. Humility is part of progress.
